---
title: "WDBX storage"
description: "Semantic retrieval and persistence, without turning scoped contracts into unlimited guarantees."
---

import { CodeBlock } from '../../components/ui';

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="retrieval-has-a-scope"><a href="#retrieval-has-a-scope">Retrieval has a scope</a></h2>

WDBX is the semantic-storage component associated with the ABI workspace. Vector retrieval helps find stored representations related to a query; similarity does not by itself establish factual correctness or permission to reveal a record.

The ABI README reports contract coverage for ordered vector-search results, metadata round trips, segment and WAL recovery, compaction, temporal-graph snapshot restore, and MCP hybrid ranking. This review did not rerun that coverage.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="persistence-must-be-explicit"><a href="#persistence-must-be-explicit">Persistence must be explicit</a></h2>

Persistence may be disabled, unavailable, or unsuccessful. The runtime should distinguish those outcomes from a successful durable write rather than manufacturing a success message. The README describes opt-out settings for applicable paths.

<CodeBlock code={"ABI_WDBX_PERSIST=0\nABI_WDBX_PATH=:memory:"} note={"These are documented configuration values, not commands that connect this website to WDBX. Their effect depends on the actual runtime path."} />

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="verify-the-guarantee-you-need"><a href="#verify-the-guarantee-you-need">Verify the guarantee you need</a></h2>

A storage recovery contract does not establish production distributed sharding, regulatory compliance, arbitrary scale, or a latency target. Evaluate the specific durability, isolation, recovery, and deployment behavior that matters to your application.

Consult the current WDBX specification and tests at the revision you will use. Record which behavior was checked and under what conditions. The conceptual explanations in this site should not be mistaken for versioned API documentation.

</section>
